content.text:
The campaign is finished, and I submitted **index 12 (V 0.858, Zr 0.142)**. It gave the highest measured photocurrent, **5.98 µA**.

I used all three merit measurements, each after the required model check:

| Index | V fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.673 (close to pure ZrV₂O₇) | 0.84 µA |
| 10 | 0.879 (the most V-rich film) | 3.73 µA |
| **12** | **0.858** | **5.98 µA** |

- **Why the V-rich end:** V₂O₅ is stable in the model check, and its predicted band gap (2.83 eV) sits well below the 3.22 eV light, so it absorbs strongly. ZrV₂O₇ is also stable, but its predicted gap (3.14 eV) is only just below the photon energy. The Zr-rich films should absorb little.
- **What the results show:** photocurrent rose sharply towards the V-rich end, but was higher at 0.858 than at the most V-rich film (0.879).
- **What I didn't test:**
  - I didn't use any XRD measurements, so the phase makeup of each film is assumed, not confirmed.
  - I never measured the Zr-rich films; I ruled them out on band gap alone.
  - Index 1 (V 0.831), the next film along from index 12, was also unmeasured, so a slightly better composition could sit there.
